comments.text: Reading this made me (very) sorely miss my A1200, which I used as my daily driver all the way up to 2003. I was shocked at how much difference in speed a 4MB Fast RAM expansion and 68881 FPU made. You might like Photon of Scoopex's Amiga Hardware Programming tutorial[1], in which he creates an Amiga Demo using assembly from scratch in ASMOne/ASMTwo [1] [VIDEO]

comments.text: I think the opposite is true because those machines were built around assembly programming. The hardware was essentially the software development framework. Check out this assembly programming series, it's less assembly code on the Amiga to get something on screen or getting mouse/keyboard input than with highlevel languages and APIs/frameworks today: [VIDEO]

comments.why: Amiga hardware programming among a list of old system videos.
comments.text: If you enjoy reading documents, BITSAVERS.ORG is a treasure mine full of lost knowledge. [LINK] Here you will find Xerox PARC, DEC, Burroughs, Apple, Sun, Borland,... old research documents, papers, manuals. In the context of static compilation, for example in MS-DOS, take Turbo Pascal 6.0 programmer's guide. [LINK] For some 8 bit love you can check ZX Spectrum and Atari archives. [LINK] [LINK] Next step is to get an emulator for any of those old OS/computers and try to follow along one of those books. Also there are some videos on YouTube showing those systems. "The Smalltalk-80 Programming System" [LINK] "NeXT vs Sun" [LINK] "Steve Jobs internal demo of NeXTSTEP 3" [LINK] "Amiga Programming" [LINK] "Amiga Hardware Programming" [VIDEO] The Mother of All Demos" [LINK] Just a very tiny sample of videos
